blocks.en: Welcome back to Michael's Morning Listening! Today we have two amazing stories: a car that can fly, and a tortoise that has lived for almost two hundred years. Let's dive in!
What if your family car could fly over a traffic jam? That sounds like science fiction, right? But it just happened in real life!

Engineers showed off a new electric sports car with ten small thrusters built into its body. These thrusters shoot out powerful bursts of compressed air — just like the ones on a spaceship. During a live show, the car drove up a huge curved ramp, kept driving while upside down, then flew into the air, did a complete barrel roll, and landed safely on its wheels. It even lifted itself over five other cars while moving!

The fastest version can go from zero to sixty miles per hour in less than one second — faster than you can say "flying car"! And it can still drive three hundred miles on one charge, just like a normal electric car.

How does it work? The secret is simple physics. When the thrusters push air down, the air pushes the car up. It is the same idea that lifts a rocket off the ground. The car also has strong fans underneath that suck air out, pressing the car tightly onto the road — that is how it can drive upside down without falling!

This car cannot fly you to school yet — the air tanks only last a few seconds. But every big invention starts with a crazy first step. The Wright brothers' first flight lasted only twelve seconds, and look where we are now. Maybe the flying cars of the future are being born right now, in front of our eyes.
Let's meet Jonathan, a giant tortoise who is now one hundred and ninety-four years old. He was born around the time the first photographs were taken — long before cars, phones, or airplanes existed!

Jonathan lives on a small island in the Atlantic Ocean called Saint Helena. He has met kings and queens, survived two world wars, and he is still slowly munching his vegetables every day, just like your grandpa — except your grandpa is probably not one hundred and ninety-four!

Scientists recently studied Jonathan's genes to learn the secrets of his super-long life. They found something amazing: the chemical patterns around his energy-making genes are unusually neat and orderly. Think of your genes as a huge library of instruction books. Over time, most people's books get messy and dog-eared. But Jonathan's books? They still look almost brand new, even after nearly two centuries!
Does this mean we can all live to two hundred? Not yet. But every clue brings scientists one step closer to understanding why some bodies age slowly — and how we might all stay healthier, longer.
Here's today's joke: What do you call a tortoise that flies? ... A "heli-tortoise"! Get it? Helicopter plus tortoise!
That brings us to the end of today's show! Before you go, here's a question: If you could invent one crazy feature for a car of the future, what would it be — and why?
Have a wonderful day, and see you tomorrow morning!
